what: Ex-US attorney general defends Epstein files handling in congressional probe

clean_source_blocks.text: Former US Attorney General Pam Bondi has defended her handling of the release of documents related to the convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. Bondi, who was removed from her post as America's top law enforcement officer by US President Donald Trump in April, testified behind closed doors on Friday in Washington DC. "We demonstrated an unprecedented commitment to transparency in the Department's search for, collection and review of the Epstein files, producing nearly three million pages of material," she said in opening remarks to the US House Oversight Committee. Bondi was formally summoned by the panel in March, just before Trump announced her ouster as his administration's top prosecutor. As attorney general, Bondi was tasked with implementing the Epstein Files Transparency Act, legislation signed into law by Trump that mandated the US Department of Justice publicly release unclassified records.
The testimony comes about a month after America's top prosecutor was ousted by US President Donald Trump.

Former U.S. Attorney General Pam Bondi (center) arrives to testify at a closed-door interview with the House Oversight Committee on Capitol Hill on Friday in Washington, D.C. Lawmakers will ask Bondi questions about the federal government's handling of the Jeffrey Epstein case and release of related files to the public. Andrew Harnik/Getty Images hide caption Former Attorney General Pam Bondi defended her handling of the Epstein files in a closed-door interview Friday before House lawmakers, noting that then-Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche oversaw the document review process. "The bottom line is: justice and transparency in this matter have been delivered at the direction of President Trump and his administration," Bondi said in a prepared opening statement obtained by NPR.

The Republican-led House Oversight Committee subpoenaed Bondi for a closed-door transcribed interview in March to discuss her role in overseeing the DOJ's release of millions of documents related to convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. "There were redaction errors," Bondi said of the released Epstein files. "But since day one of this process, this Department has been committed to accountability and transparency." Bondi said handling the release of the Epstein files was an "enormously complicated and labor-intensive process." She also said that she "did not lead every aspect" of the release or "conduct the document review" herself. Instead, she said, she "delegated oversight over this process to Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche." Blanche has been acting attorney general since Bondi was ousted from the DOJ's top spot in April.

original_article.research:
[Lähde: BBC World]
Former US Attorney General Pam Bondi has defended her handling of the release of documents related to the convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

Bondi, who was removed from her post as America's top law enforcement officer by US President Donald Trump in April, testified behind closed doors on Friday in Washington DC.

"We demonstrated an unprecedented commitment to transparency in the Department's search for, collection and review of the Epstein files, producing nearly three million pages of material," she said in opening remarks to the US House Oversight Committee.

Bondi was formally summoned by the panel in March, just before Trump announced her ouster as his administration's top prosecutor.

As attorney general, Bondi was tasked with implementing the Epstein Files Transparency Act, legislation signed into law by Trump that mandated the US Department of Justice publicly release unclassified records.

But Bondi and the US Justice Department have been widely criticised, with accusations that documents were withheld and files were published that made victims of Epstein's crimes publicly identifiable.

"I am proud of the department's record and commitment to transparency under my leadership," she said.

"This was an enormously complicated and labour-intensive process. To the best of my knowledge, the department produced everything required under the Epstein Files Transparency Act."

The committee's Republican chairman, James Comer, wrote in a subpoena letter that they were investigating the "possible mismanagement" of the Epstein investigation and compliance with the act.

Ahead of Friday's meeting, Comer told reporters that successive governments had failed Epstein's victims and that Bondi would be pressed about her handling of the release of the documents.

"We're going to try to determine whether or not there could be more documents legally turned over," Comer said. "I want every document. I don't want anything held back and I think the majority of the committee's the same way."

But three hours into the congressional interview, Democrats emerged accusing Bondi of being evasive in her answers, deferring responsibility to her former deputy, and said government lawyers had stepped in to prevent her from answering questions.

"She said she would not speak or respond to any questions that had anything to do with President Trump," said Robert Garcia, the committee's leading Democrat.

payload.title: Yhdysvaltain entinen oikeusministeri puolusti Epstein-asiakirjojen käsittelyä kongressissa
payload.summary: Yhdysvaltain entinen oikeusministeri Pam Bondi puolusti oikeusministeriön työtä Jeffrey Epsteinia koskevien asiakirjojen julkistamisessa suljetussa kuulemisessa edustajainhuoneen valvontavaliokunnassa.
payload.content:
Yhdysvaltain entinen oikeusministeri Pam Bondi on puolustanut tapaansa käsitellä Jeffrey Epsteinia koskevien asiakirjojen julkistamista kongressin valvontatutkinnassa Washingtonissa. Bondi kuultiin perjantaina suljettujen ovien takana edustajainhuoneen valvontavaliokunnassa noin kuukausi sen jälkeen, kun presidentti Donald Trump oli erottanut hänet Yhdysvaltain ylimmän lainvalvontaviranomaisen tehtävästä.

## Bondi korosti läpinäkyvyyttä

Bondin mukaan oikeusministeriö osoitti poikkeuksellista sitoutumista avoimuuteen etsiessään, kerätessään ja arvioidessaan Epstein-aineistoa. Hänen valmistelluissa avauskommenteissaan todettiin, että viranomaiset tuottivat lähes kolme miljoonaa sivua materiaalia.

Kuuleminen liittyy siihen, miten liittovaltion hallinto on käsitellyt ja julkaissut asiakirjoja, jotka koskevat seksuaalirikoksista tuomittua Jeffrey Epsteinia. Bondi oli oikeusministerinä vastuussa Epstein Files Transparency Act -lain toimeenpanosta. Trumpin allekirjoittama laki velvoitti oikeusministeriön julkaisemaan julkisesti salassa pidon ulkopuolelle jääviä asiakirjoja.

Edustajainhuoneen republikaanijohtoinen valvontavaliokunta kutsui Bondin maaliskuussa suljettuun, litteroitavaan kuulemiseen. Kutsu annettiin juuri ennen kuin Trump ilmoitti Bondin erottamisesta oikeusministeriön johdosta.

## Vastuu asiakirjaprosessista nousi esiin

Bondi myönsi, että julkaistuissa Epstein-asiakirjoissa oli peitevärimerkintöihin liittyneitä virheitä. Samalla hän sanoi, että ministeriö oli alusta lähtien sitoutunut vastuullisuuteen ja avoimuuteen.

Hänen mukaansa asiakirjojen julkaiseminen oli erittäin monimutkainen ja työvoimavaltainen prosessi. Bondi sanoi myös, ettei hän johtanut kaikkia julkaisun osa-alueita eikä tehnyt asiakirjojen arviointia itse. Sen sijaan hän kertoi delegoineensa prosessin valvontaa apulaisoikeusministeri Todd Blanchelle.

Blanche on toiminut oikeusministerinä Bondin erottamisen jälkeen. Bondin mukaan Epstein-aineiston käsittelyssä on hänen näkökulmastaan toteutettu sekä oikeutta että läpinäkyvyyttä Trumpin ja tämän hallinnon ohjauksessa.

Suljettu kuuleminen antaa kongressin jäsenille mahdollisuuden kysyä Bondilta suoraan hänen roolistaan asiakirjojen julkaisussa. Huomio on kohdistunut erityisesti siihen, miten laajaa aineistoa on käsitelty, kuka prosessia johti ja miksi julkaisuissa ilmeni virheitä.
summary_bullets: Pam Bondi kuultiin suljetussa kuulemisessa edustajainhuoneen valvontavaliokunnassa Washingtonissa.
Bondi puolusti oikeusministeriön työtä Epstein-asiakirjojen etsimisessä, arvioinnissa ja julkistamisessa.
Hän myönsi julkaisuissa olleen peitevärimerkintöihin liittyneitä virheitä, mutta korosti avoimuutta ja vastuullisuutta.
Bondi sanoi delegoineensa prosessin valvontaa apulaisoikeusministeri Todd Blanchelle.
payload.journalist_note: Artikkeli perustuu paketissa olleisiin BBC:n ja NPR:n tietoihin. Väitteet on rajattu kuulemiseen, Bondin lausuntoihin, asiakirjaprosessiin ja tiedossa olevaan viranomaisrooliin; uutta taustaa tai päätelmiä ei lisätty.
